title: Inspect browser page target
description: Inspect one opaque target at an exact page revision. Returns bounded local structure and geometry; never returns selectors, action coordinates, scripts, or unbounded DOM.
guidance: A text field's value is returned only when the page produced it (a read-only or disabled field, an output) or you typed into the field with dsagent.page.action in this page, which the page may since have rewritten with its result; never a credential, one-time code or payment field.

pageContextId.description: Opaque page context from dsagent.pages.list, dsagent.page.open, or a receipt's destinationPageContextId.

targetId.description: Opaque target identifier returned by dsagent.page.observe.

expectedRevision.description: Observed revision associated with the target; local identity and context must remain valid.

inputSchema.description: Opaque target binding and revision guard for one bounded structure inspection.

revision.description: Revision to which all returned evidence is bound.

filled.description: Whether an editable target contains a value, without returning the value.

checked.description: Whether a checkbox-like target is checked.

selected.description: Whether a selectable target is selected.

current.description: Whether the target is marked as current.

expanded.description: Whether an expandable target is expanded.

sort.description: Bounded sort direction when exposed by the page.

state.description: Allowlisted target state without field values.

x.description: Target left position in current CSS viewport pixels; evidence only, never accepted as action input.

y.description: Target top position in current CSS viewport pixels; evidence only, never accepted as action input.

rect.description: Current target geometry for observation only.

relation.description: Target relation to the current viewport.

occlusion.description: Conservative center-point occlusion summary; unknown means the runtime could not prove visibility.

items.description: Bounded semantic summary of a nearby node without selectors or arbitrary attributes.

relation.description: Sibling direction relative to the target.

role.description: Bounded sibling semantic role when available.

label.description: Bounded sibling visible label when available.

content.description: Target-local allowlisted HTML evidence, capped at 4096 UTF-8 bytes by the owner.

truncated.description: Whether optional neighbor or ancestor evidence was removed to fit the byte budget.

localDom.description: Bounded local structure without selectors, values, script, style, or arbitrary attributes.

value.description: The field's current text when it is readable: a page-produced field (read-only, disabled, output) or one you typed into with dsagent.page.action; absent otherwise.

textColor.description: Current computed CSS color in the target document, including inherited rules. Not final composited pixel color.

backgroundColor.description: Current computed CSS background-color of this element; may be transparent. Does not inspect backgrounds behind it.

appearance.description: Fixed computed color evidence for this target only. No arbitrary CSS, custom properties, URLs, pixels or private field values. Absent when unavailable.

outcome.description: labelled: a label element, a heading or a kept hint names the field; unlabelled: none.

stop.description: Why the search ended: own-label (a <label>/aria-labelledby), heading (a short label before the field or its column), hint-kept (a long line above, no short label beside), fieldset (its legend), list-entry, readout (a value, not words), other-field-heading, section-fields (an ancestor holds more than three fields), section-size (an ancestor holds more than 250 elements), depth (eight levels with earlier siblings read, or 24 ancestors climbed), body, control-strip.

depth.description: The ancestor level where the search ended (0 is the field's parent).

labelChars.description: Rendered characters of the attached label, when there is one.

levels.description: Each ancestor level climbed, nearest first.

siblings.description: The earlier siblings read at this level, nearest first.

kind.description: What the sibling read as: label (short words), long-line, readout, control-inside (holds a button, link or other control, so it is no label), too-long, empty, hidden, list-entry, field, field-block, control-strip.

items.description: One earlier sibling, as the search read it.
One ancestor level of the search.

fieldLabelSearch.description: For a value field: why its label search (the fieldLabel find and observe report) ended where it did. Typed facts, no text.

evidenceGaps.description: Bounded technical evidence gaps derived from current page facts; never a business-risk judgment.

kind.description: Read-only evidence layer most likely to close the technical gap; bring-forward (with PAGE_NOT_RENDERED) means the browser is not rendering the page: dsagent.page.focus brings it forward, then observe again.

reason.description: Technical evidence gap that caused this recommendation.

expectedRevision.description: Exact revision to reuse for the next read.

targetId.description: Optional opaque target for target-scoped evidence.

recommendedObservation.description: Bounded advisory only; it never captures an image or executes an action.

guidance.description: Optional owner-derived read-only evidence escalation guidance.

status.description: no-wall: the monitor checked this page and found no sign-in or verification wall, so do not tell the person the site needs a sign-in. sign-in-required: the page asks the person to sign in or pass a verification (the browser's sign-in monitor, the one workflow runs use, decided it).

type.description: The kind of wall the monitor recognised: a challenge (CAPTCHA, SLIDER_CAPTCHA, IMAGE_CAPTCHA, RECAPTCHA, HCAPTCHA, TURNSTILE, GEETEST, ARKOSE, CLOUDFLARE, BOT_PROTECTION) or a sign-in kind (LOGIN_FORM, PHONE_LOGIN, SSO, OTP…).

waitingOn.description: Who the wall waits on. agent: a challenge you hold and pass yourself with page actions (see the field description). person: a sign-in wall, or a challenge you failed; DSphere handed it to the person. DSphere has shown the person its sign-in sheet for this page (and a desktop notification when its side panel is closed). Tell your user that the page needs them to sign in or pass the check in the browser and click Resume in the DSphere side panel; do not use dsagent.page.ask for it. Wait, then read this page again (dsagent.page.observe); continue the task where it stopped once authentication is absent. Do not end the task, retry the effect before then, or sign in, enter credentials or solve the challenge yourself.

attemptsLeft.description: With waitingOn agent: effect calls (dsagent.page.action / .actions) you may still spend on this challenge before it is the person's.

authentication.description: The sign-in monitor's verdict on the page: status no-wall when it checked and found none (absent when it could not check); status sign-in-required, with type and confidence, when the page is a sign-in or verification (CAPTCHA) wall. With waitingOn "agent" the wall is a human-verification challenge (a CAPTCHA or bot check) that you pass yourself, with the page gestures a person uses: dsagent.page.visual.observe shows the puzzle; dsagent.page.observe / dsagent.page.find list its controls (a checkbox or a picture tile: click; a slider knob: drag with delta or dropTargetId; a code field: type; a refresh or confirm control: click); then read the page again. Once the challenge has survived one of your answers, DSphere sends your drags and plain clicks on it as real browser input (the receipt says so); nothing changes in how you call them. authentication absent or no-wall means it is passed; continue the task. You have attemptsLeft effect calls on this challenge (12 at first) and 5 minutes; when they are spent, or you call dsagent.page.notify on this page because you cannot pass it, DSphere hands the challenge to the person and waitingOn becomes "person". Never enter credentials, sign in or ask the person before that. The person may turn this off (DSphere Settings → Verification Challenges; dsagent.settings.get section agent-challenge-walls, which you cannot change): then every wall is the person's from the start. With waitingOn "person" effects other than a click on the active surface's own close control (activeSurface.closeTargetId), dismiss, scroll and Escape are refused with TARGET_BUSY / AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED until the wall is gone. You may still close a sign-in popup the way a guest does, which signs nothing in: click its own close control (activeSurface.closeTargetId of your latest page read), dismiss, scroll or press Escape; then read the page again. DSphere has shown the person its sign-in sheet for this page (and a desktop notification when its side panel is closed). Tell your user that the page needs them to sign in or pass the check in the browser and click Resume in the DSphere side panel; do not use dsagent.page.ask for it. Wait, then read this page again (dsagent.page.observe); continue the task where it stopped once authentication is absent. Do not end the task, retry the effect before then, or sign in, enter credentials or solve the challenge yourself.

outputSchema.description: Revision-bound target-local structure and geometry evidence.
